subject: Stacking Points on Y Axis defined by Variable Names

messages.author: 461a7a91b2b3d3a1
messages.subject: Stacking Points on Y Axis defined by Variable Names
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to come up with a function that will display regression
coefficients along with uncertainty using ggplot. Essentially, this
function is intended to work much like the "coefplot" command in
Andrew Gelman's ARM package, but made with ggplot and with a bit more
flexibility to plot coefficients by group.

Ideally, what I'd like to be able to do is clearly display stacked
coefficients from separate model runs (e.g. unadjusted and adjusted),
but keep the same overall faceting.

With the code and function below you can see what I am talking about.

if you look at the plot this code produces, the problem is that each
coefficient is plotted at the same y value (which in this case is the
variable name, not a number), making it a bit difficult to really see
the uncertainty bands. What I'd like to do is, stack the two
coefficient points somewhat so they don't overlap with one another.
Anyone know how to do this?

Thanks!
John G.

library(ggplot2)
coefplot<-
function(coefs,se,varnames,category1,trans=0.4,category2,category3,xlabel="X
Label",vline=0) {
indata <-
data.frame(varnames,category1,category2,coefs,se,category3); indata
indata.1 <- indata.2 <- indata
indata.1$x <- indata.1$coefs - 1.96 * indata.1$se
indata.2$x <- indata.1$coefs + 1.96 * indata.1$se
indata.1$x2 <- indata.1$coefs - 1 * indata.1$se
indata.2$x2 <- indata.1$coefs + 1 * indata.1$se
indata <- rbind(indata.1,indata.2)
range <- range(indata$x)
lim <- c(range[1]-range[1]*.1,range[2]+range[2]*.1)
plot <-
ggplot(indata,aes(x=x,y=varnames,color=category2),title="test")
+geom_point(aes(x=coefs),position="identity")
+facet_grid(category1~category3,scales="free",space="free"); plot
plot+facet_wrap(~category3)
plot <- plot + geom_line(,alpha=trans) + xlim(range) +
labs(y="Variable Name",x=xlabel); plot
plot <- plot + geom_line(aes(x=x2),alpha=min(1,trans*1.5)) +
opts(panel.grid.minor=theme_blank()); plot
plot <- plot + theme_set(theme_bw())
+opts(panel.grid.minor=theme_blank())
+geom_vline(xintercept=vline,color=gray,lty=2,alpha=.5)+
opts(strip.text.y = theme_text());plot


return(plot)
}

n <- 10
varnames <- paste("Variable",seq(1:(n)),sep=" ")
cat1 <- sample(c("Income\nVariables","Demographic
\nVariables"),n,replace=TRUE)

model.1 <-
data.frame(varnames,cat1,coef=runif(n,min=0,max=2),se=runif(n,min=0,max=1),time="Model
1",group="Subset A")
model.2 <-
data.frame(varnames,cat1,coef=runif(n,min=0,max=2),se=runif(n,min=0,max=1),time="Model
2",group="Subset A")
model.3 <-
data.frame(varnames,cat1,coef=runif(n,min=0,max=2),se=runif(n,min=0,max=1),time="Model
1",group="Subset B")
model.4 <-
data.frame(varnames,cat1,coef=runif(n,min=0,max=2),se=runif(n,min=0,max=1),time="Model
2",group="Subset B")

results <- rbind(model.1,model.2,model.3, model.4)
is.factor(results$se)
table(results$time)

coefplot(coefs=results$coef,se=results$se,varnames=results
$varnames,category1=factor(results$cat1),category2=factor(results
$time),category3=factor(results$group))

Have you tried setting the width argument manually? I think the
problem may be that by default ggplot2 tries to dodge geoms based on how
wide it thinks they are, which is 0 (or very narrow at least) in the
case of a point or a linerange ...

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Stacking Points on Y Axis defined by Variable Names
parts:
Hi John:

Thank you for the support :)  The closest I've been able to come to dodging points by factor level is shown below in the following toy example:

d2 <- data.frame(junk = rnorm(3000, mean = rep(1:3, 100)),
                 x = factor(rep(1:3, 100)),
                 z = factor(rep(rep(c('A', 'B', 'C', 'D'), each = 250), 3)))
g <- ggplot(d2, aes(x = x, y = junk))
g + geom_boxplot(aes(fill = z), position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = z), size = 1, color = 'blue',
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.8))

I thought I could only get away with it for two groups, but was pleasantly surprised to see it work for four, so it's a start.

One application I had in mind for dodging points by factor levels was to add points to a boxplot or related distribution plots such as violin or bean plots - alternatively, augmenting CIs at levels of factor 2 with corresponding point scatters for each level of factor 1.

The problem I have with the plot above is the inability to control the amount of jitter in the points - I would have preferred a tighter scatter around the whiskers of the box plot. As far as I can tell, using position_dodge() on the points eliminates the ability to control the jitter with position_jitter(). I tried to add them both inside a list ('lattice-like'), but no...  :) It's entirely possible that I'm missing something 'obvious' in ggplot2, though.

In hierarchical data structures, the ability to be able to 'drill down' graphically to at least two levels is very useful, and I think there are some opportunities to create insightful visual metaphors for this type of data; as far as I can tell, there isn't much available at present.

HTH,
Dennis

parts:
Hi Dennis and Ben,

Thanks again to you both. Dennis, this looks really intriguing; I
will try it out.

In any case, I think I have found a workaround for my problem -- it's
not too elegant yet, but it seems to work. The idea is to to use a
continuous y scaling, rather than the default discrete scaling that is
used when one of the axes has levels of a factor. By changing things
in this way one can then just systematically "jitter" the y values
around each break point.

I haven't had a chance to generalize into a function yet, and the
coding could certainly be improved, but the following seems to work
for jittering each coefficient around its variable name on the y axis:

n <- 10
varnames <- paste("Variable",seq(1:(n)),sep=" ")
cat1 <- sample(c("Income\nVariables","Demographic
\nVariables"),n,replace=TRUE)

model.1 <-
data.frame(varnames,cat1,coef=runif(n,min=0,max=2),se=runif(n,min=0,max=1),time="Model
1",group="Subset A")
model.2 <-
data.frame(varnames,cat1,coef=runif(n,min=0,max=2),se=runif(n,min=0,max=1),time="Model
2",group="Subset A")
model.3 <-
data.frame(varnames,cat1,coef=runif(n,min=0,max=2),se=runif(n,min=0,max=1),time="Model
1",group="Subset B")
model.4 <-
data.frame(varnames,cat1,coef=runif(n,min=0,max=2),se=runif(n,min=0,max=1),time="Model
2",group="Subset B")

results <- rbind(model.1,model.2,model.3, model.4)

head(results)

varcats <- levels(results$cat1); varcats
n <- 0
name <- c()
num <- c()
for (i in 1:length(varcats)) {
foo <- table(results[results$cat1==varcats[i],]$varnames)>0; foo
foo2 <- factor(names(foo[foo==TRUE])); foo2
name <- c(name,levels(foo2)) ; name
num <- c(num,as.numeric(foo2)+n); num
n <- n + length(foo2); n
}
vars <- data.frame(name,num)
names(vars) <- c("varnames","varno")
results <- merge(results,vars,by="varnames")

for( j in 1:length(levels(results$time))) {
if (j==1) {
results[results$time==levels(results$time)[j],]$varno <-
results[results$time==levels(results$time)[j],]$varno+.15
}
if (j==2) {
results[results$time==levels(results$time)[j],]$varno <-
results[results$time==levels(results$time)[j],]$varno-.15
}
}
plot <- ggplot(results,aes(x=coef,y=varno,color=time))
+geom_point(aes(x=coef))
+facet_grid(cat1~group,scales="free_y",space="free"); plot
plot + scale_y_continuous(breaks=vars$varno,labels=vars$varnames)
